title: 是 sentences
pattern: A 是 B / A 不是 B
explanation: Use 是 to say that A is B, for identity or category. To negate it, put 不 before 是: 不是.

examples.pinyin: wǒ shì xué shēng
examples.en: I am a student.

examples.pinyin: tā shì wǒ de lǎo shī
examples.en: She is my teacher.

examples.pinyin: dà wèi bú shì zhōng guó rén
examples.en: David is not Chinese.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ hěn gāoxìng.
mistake.en: I'm happy.
mistake.reason: 是 links nouns, not adjectives; use 很 with an adjective and no 是.

title: 有 for having
pattern: Subject + 有 + Noun / Subject + 没有 + Noun
explanation: Use 有 (yǒu) to say someone has something. To negate it, use 没有 (méiyǒu), never 不有.

examples.pinyin: wǒ yǒu liǎng gè gēge。
examples.en: I have two older brothers.

examples.pinyin: tā méiyǒu shǒujī。
examples.en: He doesn't have a cell phone.

examples.pinyin: nǐ yǒu diànnǎo ma?
examples.en: Do you have a computer?

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ méiyǒu qián.
mistake.en: I don't have any money.
mistake.reason: 有 is negated with 没有, never with 不.

title: Place + 有 / 是 + thing
pattern: Place + 有 + number + measure word + noun / Place + 是 + noun
explanation: Use 有 to say that a place has something in it (there is/are). Use 是 to say that a place is exactly that thing, often when it is the only thing there.

examples.pinyin: wǒ jiā yǒu sān gè rén
examples.en: My home has three people.

examples.pinyin: xué xiào lǐ yǒu yí gè shū diàn
examples.en: There is a bookstore in the school.

examples.pinyin: xué xiào qián biān shì yī yuàn
examples.en: In front of the school is a hospital.

mistake.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng yǒu sān běn shū.
mistake.en: There are three books on the table.
mistake.reason: When saying a place has a number of things, use 有, not 是.

title: 在 + place
pattern: S + 在 + place (+ verb)
explanation: 在 means 'to be at' when it is the main verb. Before another verb it is a preposition: put 在 + place before the verb to say where the action happens.

examples.pinyin: wǒ zài jiā
examples.en: I'm at home.

examples.pinyin: bàba zài gōngsī gōngzuò
examples.en: Dad works at a company.

examples.pinyin: wǒmen zài xuéxiào xuéxí hànyǔ
examples.en: We study Chinese at school.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ zài fàndiàn chī fàn.
mistake.en: I'm eating at a restaurant.
mistake.reason: The 在 + place phrase must come before the verb, not after it.

title: 吗 questions
pattern: Statement + 吗?
explanation: Add 吗 to the end of a statement to turn it into a yes/no question. Keep the word order the same as in English statements; just put 吗 at the end.

examples.pinyin: nǐ shì xué shēng ma?
examples.en: Are you a student?

examples.pinyin: nǐ xǐ huan chī miàn tiáor ma?
examples.en: Do you like eating noodles?

examples.pinyin: jīn tiān hěn lěng ma?
examples.en: Is it very cold today?

mistake.pinyin: Nǐ shì lǎoshī ma?
mistake.en: Are you a teacher?
mistake.reason: 吗 must go at the very end of the sentence, not in the middle.

title: Question words
pattern: Subject + Verb + Question word (in the answer's position)
explanation: In Chinese, a question word like 什么, 谁, 哪儿, 几 or 多少 goes exactly where the answer would go. You do not move it to the front like in English, and you do not add 吗.

examples.pinyin: nǐ xiǎng chī shén me?
examples.en: What do you want to eat?

examples.pinyin: nǐ jiā zài nǎr?
examples.en: Where is your home?

examples.pinyin: zhè ge duō shao qián?
examples.en: How much is this?

mistake.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng chī shénme?
mistake.en: What do you want to eat?
mistake.reason: The question word stays in the position of the answer (after the verb), not at the start like in English.

title: A-not-A questions
pattern: V + 不 + V (+ object)? / Adj + 不 + Adj / 有没有 + object
explanation: To ask a yes/no question, repeat the verb or adjective with 不 in between instead of adding 吗. For 有, use 有没有 (not 有不有).

examples.pinyin: nǐ qù bu qù chāoshì?
examples.en: Are you going to the supermarket?

examples.pinyin: zhège cài hǎochī bu hǎochī?
examples.en: Is this dish tasty?

examples.pinyin: nǐ yǒu méiyǒu shǒujī?
examples.en: Do you have a cell phone?

mistake.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan bù xǐhuan hē chá?
mistake.en: Do you like drinking tea or not?
mistake.reason: An A-not-A question already asks the question, so do not add 吗 at the end.

title: 呢 questions
pattern: A，B 呢？ / Noun + 呢？
explanation: Add 呢 after a noun to ask 'and what about…?' after a topic is already set. It also asks 'where is…?' when a thing or person is missing.

examples.pinyin: wǒ hěn hǎo, nǐ ne?
examples.en: I'm fine, and you?

examples.pinyin: wǒ xǐhuan hē chá, nǐ ne?
examples.en: I like drinking tea, how about you?

examples.pinyin: wǒ de shǒujī ne?
examples.en: Where is my phone?

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī ne?
mistake.en: Where's my phone?
mistake.reason: Don't combine 呢 with 吗; 呢 alone after the noun already asks 'where is it?'.

title: 不 vs 没
pattern: 不 + verb/adj (present, future, habit, adjective) ; 没(有) + verb (past) ; 没有 = don't have
explanation: Use 不 to negate habits, future plans, present wishes and adjectives. Use 没 or 没有 to say something did not happen in the past, and to negate 有 (没有, never 不有).

examples.pinyin: wǒ bù hē chá
examples.en: I don't drink tea.

examples.pinyin: tā zuó tiān méi shàng bān
examples.en: He didn't go to work yesterday.

examples.pinyin: wǒ méi yǒu shǒu jī
examples.en: I don't have a cell phone.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān méi qù chāoshì.
mistake.en: I didn't go to the supermarket yesterday.
mistake.reason: For a past action that did not happen, use 没, not 不.

title: 的 for possession
pattern: Noun/Pronoun + 的 + Noun
explanation: Use 的 after a person or noun to show who owns something, like 's in English. With family and close relations, 的 is usually dropped (我妈妈, not 我的妈妈).

examples.pinyin: zhè shì wǒ de shǒu jī
examples.en: This is my phone.

examples.pinyin: nà shì lǎo shī de shū
examples.en: That is the teacher's book.

examples.pinyin: wǒ mā ma zài jiā
examples.en: My mom is at home.

mistake.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de shǒujī.
mistake.en: This is my phone.
mistake.reason: Use 的 between a pronoun and an ordinary object; only family and close relations can drop it.

title: Measure words
pattern: 数字/这/那/哪 + 量词 + 名词（两 + 量词）
explanation: In Chinese, a number or 这/那/哪 must be followed by a measure word before the noun, like 三个人 or 这本书. Use 两, not 二, before a measure word to say 'two'.

examples.pinyin: wǒ yǒu liǎng gè hái zi
examples.en: I have two children.

examples.pinyin: zhè běn shū hěn hǎo kàn
examples.en: This book is very good-looking (nice to read).

examples.pinyin: nǐ xǐ huan nǎ jiàn yī fu
examples.en: Which piece of clothing do you like?

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng ge píngguǒ.
mistake.en: I bought two apples.
mistake.reason: Use 两, not 二, before a measure word when counting quantity.

title: Adjectives as predicates
pattern: Subject + 很 + Adj / Subject + 不 + Adj
explanation: In Chinese, adjectives work as verbs, so you do not use 是 before them. Put 很 before the adjective in a plain statement (it is often weak, like 'is'), and use 不 directly before the adjective to negate.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān hěn lěng.
examples.en: It is cold today.

examples.pinyin: Zhège miànbāo hěn hǎochī.
examples.en: This bread is delicious.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài bù máng.
examples.en: I am not busy now.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ hěn máng.
mistake.en: I'm busy.
mistake.reason: Adjectives are not used with 是; just say subject + 很 + adjective.

title: 很 · 太…了 · 真 · 非常
pattern: 很/非常 + adj; 太 + adj + 了; 真 + adj
explanation: Put 很 or 非常 before an adjective to say 'very' or 'extremely'. Use 太…了 for 'too/so' and 真 for a feeling or exclamation like 'really!'.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān hěn lěng.
examples.en: It's very cold today.

examples.pinyin: Zhège bāozi tài hǎochī le!
examples.en: This baozi is so delicious!

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de diànnǎo zhēn piàoliang!
examples.en: Your computer is really nice!

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ hěn máng.
mistake.en: I'm busy.
mistake.reason: Do not use 是 before an adjective; the degree adverb 很 links the subject and the adjective.

title: 有点儿 + adjective
pattern: S + 有点儿 + adj
explanation: 有点儿 goes before an adjective to mean 'a bit' or 'somewhat', and it usually shows you are not happy about something. It sounds like a mild complaint.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān yǒudiǎnr lěng.
examples.en: It's a bit cold today.

examples.pinyin: Zhège dōngxi yǒudiǎnr guì.
examples.en: This thing is a bit expensive.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān yǒudiǎnr máng.
examples.en: I'm a bit busy today.

mistake.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ zǎo yìdiǎnr qǐchuáng.
mistake.en: Please get up a little earlier.
mistake.reason: 有点儿 describes a negative state; to ask for 'a little more' of something, use adj + 一点儿 instead.

title: 也 and 都
pattern: Subject + 也都 + Verb/Adj
explanation: Both 也 (also) and 都 (all) go after the subject and before the verb or adjective. When you use them together, the order is always 也都, never 都也.

examples.pinyin: wǒ men yě dōu xǐ huan chī jiǎo zi 。
examples.en: We all like eating dumplings too.

examples.pinyin: tā men yě dōu shì xué sheng 。
examples.en: They are all students too.

examples.pinyin: wǒ de péng you yě dōu hěn máng 。
examples.en: My friends are all busy too.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒmen yě dōu xǐhuan hē chá.
mistake.en: We all like drinking tea too.
mistake.reason: When combined, 也 must come before 都, so the order is 也都.

title: 会 · 能 · 可以
pattern: S + 会/能/可以 + V (+ O)
explanation: 会 means you know how to do something because you learned it. 能 means you are able to because of ability or circumstances. 可以 means you are allowed to or it is okay to.

examples.pinyin: wǒ huì shuō hàn yǔ
examples.en: I can speak Chinese (I have learned how).

examples.pinyin: nǐ míng tiān néng lái ma
examples.en: Can you come tomorrow?

examples.pinyin: wǒ kě yǐ zuò zhè lǐ ma
examples.en: May I sit here?

mistake.wrong: 我今天病了,不会去学校。
mistake.right: 我今天病了,不能去学校。
mistake.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān bìng le, bù néng qù xuéxiào.
mistake.en: I'm sick today, so I can't go to school.
mistake.reason: Being unable to go because of circumstances (illness) needs 能, not 会, which is for learned skills.

title: 想 and 要
pattern: 我想 + verb / 我要 + verb / 我要 + noun
explanation: 想 + verb softly says what you would like to do. 要 + verb says you want to or will do something more firmly, and 要 + noun means you want that thing.

examples.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng hē shuǐ
examples.en: I would like to drink some water.

examples.pinyin: wǒ míng tiān yào shàng bān
examples.en: I have to go to work tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: wǒ yào yì bēi chá
examples.en: I want a cup of tea.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ yào yì bēi chá.
mistake.en: I want a cup of tea.
mistake.reason: Before a noun, use 要 to mean want; 想 needs a verb after it.

title: Verb + 了 (completed)
pattern: Subject + Verb + 了 (+ Object) / Subject + 没 + Verb
explanation: Put 了 right after a verb to show the action was completed. To say it did not happen, use 没 before the verb and drop 了.

examples.pinyin: wǒ chī le liǎng ge bāo zi
examples.en: I ate two baozi.

examples.pinyin: zuó tiān wǒ mǎi le yí jiàn yī fu
examples.en: Yesterday I bought a piece of clothing.

examples.pinyin: tā méi hē niú nǎi
examples.en: He didn't drink milk.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ méi chī zǎofàn.
mistake.en: I didn't eat breakfast.
mistake.reason: With 没 the action did not happen, so you do not add 了 after the verb.

title: Sentence 了 (new situation)
pattern: Sentence + 了 (change / new situation)
explanation: Put 了 at the end of a sentence to show that something has changed or a new situation has begun. It often means "now it is the case that..." or "has become".

examples.pinyin: xià yǔ le , wǒ men huí jiā ba 。
examples.en: It's raining now, let's go home.

examples.pinyin: xiàn zài bā diǎn le 。
examples.en: It's already eight o'clock now.

examples.pinyin: wǒ bù xiǎng chī le 。
examples.en: I don't want to eat anymore.

mistake.pinyin: Tiānqì lěng le.
mistake.en: It's gotten cold.
mistake.reason: 了 for a new situation goes at the end; don't add 很 after it.

title: 在 / 正在 … 呢
pattern: S + 在/正在 + V (+ O) (+ 呢)
explanation: Put 在 or 正在 before a verb to say an action is happening right now. You can add 呢 at the end of the sentence to make it sound more natural.

examples.pinyin: wǒ zài chī fàn ne
examples.en: I'm eating right now.

examples.pinyin: māma zhèngzài zuò fàn
examples.en: Mom is cooking right now.

examples.pinyin: tāmen zài kàn diànshì ne
examples.en: They are watching TV.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ zài chī fàn ne.
mistake.en: I'm eating.
mistake.reason: 在 goes before the verb; 呢 goes at the end.

title: Separable verbs
pattern: V + 了 + duration + O (separable verb split)
explanation: Words like 上课, 看病 and 下课 are verb + object. Put 了 and time lengths between the two parts, not after the whole word.

examples.zh: 我今天上了两个小时课。
examples.pinyin: wǒ jīntiān shàng le liǎng gè xiǎoshí kè
examples.en: Today I had two hours of class.

examples.pinyin: yīshēng kàn le yí gè xiǎoshí bìng
examples.en: The doctor saw patients for an hour.

examples.pinyin: xià le kè, wǒ qù chī fàn
examples.en: After class ended, I went to eat.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ shàng le liǎng ge xiǎoshí kè.
mistake.en: I had two hours of class.
mistake.reason: Split 上课 and put 了 and the duration between 上 and 课.

title: Two verbs in a row
pattern: Subject + V1 (+ place) + V2 (+ object)
explanation: Chinese can put two verbs next to each other without any linking word. The first verb is the way or the place you go, and the second is the purpose: 去商店买东西 means go to the store to buy things.

examples.pinyin: wǒ qù shāngdiàn mǎi dōngxi
examples.en: I go to the store to buy things.

examples.pinyin: tā zuò chūzūchē qù xuéxiào
examples.en: He takes a taxi to school.

examples.pinyin: míngtiān wǒmen lái nǐ jiā chī fàn
examples.en: Tomorrow we are coming to your home to eat.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ qù shāngdiàn mǎi dōngxi.
mistake.en: I'm going to the store to buy things.
mistake.reason: Do not add 要 or any linking word between the two verbs; just place them in a row.

title: Two objects
pattern: Subject + 给/问 + person + thing
explanation: Some verbs take two objects: first the person, then the thing. With 给 you give something to someone; with 问 you ask someone a question.

examples.pinyin: wǒ gěi nǐ yì běn shū
examples.en: I give you a book.

examples.pinyin: tā gěi wǒ liǎng gè bāozi
examples.en: He gives me two steamed buns.

examples.pinyin: wǒ wèn lǎoshī yí gè wèntí
examples.en: I ask the teacher a question.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ yì běn shū.
mistake.en: I'm giving you a book.
mistake.reason: The person must come right after the verb, before the thing, as in English "give you a book".

title: Time and place before the verb
pattern: Subject + Time + Place + Verb (dates: 年 月 号 星期 点)
explanation: In Chinese, time words and place words come before the verb, with time first and then place. Dates and times go from big to small: year, month, day, weekday, hour.

examples.pinyin: wǒ míng tiān zài jiā gōng zuò
examples.en: I work at home tomorrow.

examples.zh: 我们今天下午在学校学习。
examples.pinyin: wǒ men jīn tiān xià wǔ zài xué xiào xué xí
examples.en: We study at school this afternoon.

examples.zh: 他明年一月三号去中国。
examples.pinyin: tā míng nián yī yuè sān hào qù zhōng guó
examples.en: He is going to China on January 3rd next year.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān zài jiā gōngzuò.
mistake.en: I'm working at home tomorrow.
mistake.reason: Time must come before place, and both must come before the verb.

title: Prices
pattern: 这个 + 多少钱？ / 数字 + 块 (+ 数字)
explanation: Ask a price with 多少钱. Say amounts with 块 (or 元 in writing); in speech a last digit after 块 means 毛, e.g. 两块五 is 2.5 yuan. Use 两, not 二, before 块 when it is the first number.

examples.pinyin: zhè ge duōshao qián
examples.en: How much is this?

examples.pinyin: píngguǒ shí kuài qián
examples.en: The apples are ten yuan.

examples.pinyin: yì bēi chá liǎng kuài wǔ
examples.en: A cup of tea is 2.5 yuan.

mistake.pinyin: Zhè ge liǎng kuài wǔ.
mistake.en: This one is two and a half yuan.
mistake.reason: Before 块 use 两, not 二, for the number 2.

title: 第 + number
pattern: 第 + number (+ measure word) + noun
explanation: Put 第 before a number to make an ordinal: 第一 means first, 第二 means second. You can add a measure word and noun after it, like 第二个星期 or 第三天.

examples.pinyin: jīn tiān shì wǒ dì yī tiān shàng bān。
examples.en: Today is my first day of work.

examples.zh: 这是我第二个星期学汉语。
examples.pinyin: zhè shì wǒ dì èr gè xīng qī xué hàn yǔ。
examples.en: This is my second week learning Chinese.

examples.pinyin: dì sān kè hěn hǎo wánr。
examples.en: Lesson three is a lot of fun.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ shì dì sān ge xuésheng.
mistake.en: I'm the third student.
mistake.reason: 第 must come before the number and the measure word, not after the number.

title: Location words
pattern: Noun + 上/下/里/外/前/后 (+ 边)
explanation: Put a location word after a noun to say where something is: 上 (on), 下 (under), 里 (inside), 外 (outside), 前 (in front), 后 (behind). 边 can be added, as in 学校前边.

examples.pinyin: Shǒujī zài zhuōzi shàng.
examples.en: The phone is on the table.

examples.pinyin: Māma zài jiā lǐ zuò fàn.
examples.en: Mom is cooking at home.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài xuéxiào qián bian.
examples.en: He is in front of the school.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ de shū zài zhuōzi shàng.
mistake.en: My book is on the table.
mistake.reason: After a noun like 桌子, you need a location word such as 上 to say where something is.

title: 和 and 对
pattern: A 和 B + verb; A 对 B + 很 + adj
explanation: 和 links two nouns, meaning 'and' or 'with'. 对 marks the target of an attitude, so 对 + person + adj means 'to/for someone'.

examples.pinyin: wǒ hé péngyou qù kàn diànyǐng。
examples.en: I go to see a movie with my friend.

examples.pinyin: lǎoshī duì wǒmen hěn hǎo。
examples.en: The teacher is very good to us.

examples.pinyin: māma hé bàba dōu zài jiā。
examples.en: Mom and Dad are both at home.

mistake.pinyin: Tā duì wǒ hěn hǎo.
mistake.en: He is very good to me.
mistake.reason: 对 + person must come before the adjective, not after it.

title: 请 and 不要
pattern: 请 + verb (please ...) / 不要 + verb (don't ...)
explanation: Put 请 before a verb to make a polite request. Put 不要 before a verb to tell someone not to do something.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zuò.
examples.en: Please sit down.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng hē chá.
examples.en: Please have some tea.

examples.pinyin: Búyào shuōhuà.
examples.en: Don't talk.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng búyào dǎ diànhuà.
examples.en: Please don't make phone calls.

mistake.pinyin: Qǐng zuò.
mistake.en: Please sit down.
mistake.reason: Use 请 alone to say 'please sit'; 不要 means 'don't', so 不要请坐 would mean 'don't please sit'. For a polite 'don't', say 请不要 + verb.

title: …，也… · …，还…
pattern: S + V/Adj，也 + V/Adj ；S + V + O，还 + V + O
explanation: 也 means 'also' and links a new subject or action to something already said. 还 means 'in addition' and adds another item or action by the same subject. Both go before the verb.

examples.pinyin: wǒ xǐhuan chá, tā yě xǐhuan chá.
examples.en: I like tea, and he likes tea too.

examples.zh: 我想吃面条儿，还想喝牛奶。
examples.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng chī miàntiáor, hái xiǎng hē niúnǎi.
examples.en: I want to eat noodles, and I also want to drink milk.

examples.pinyin: jīntiān hěn lěng, hái xiàyǔ.
examples.en: It's cold today, and it's also raining.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan chá, tā yě xǐhuan.
mistake.en: I like tea, and he does too.
mistake.reason: 也 must go after the subject and right before the verb, not before the subject.

title: 比 comparisons
pattern: A 比 B + adj (+ 一点儿 / 多了 / number + measure)
explanation: Use 比 to compare two things: A 比 B + adjective. Add 一点儿 for 'a little', 多了 for 'much', or an exact amount after the adjective. Never put 很 before the adjective in a 比 sentence.

examples.pinyin: Gēge bǐ wǒ dà liǎng suì.
examples.en: My older brother is two years older than me.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān lěng duō le.
examples.en: Today is much colder than yesterday.

examples.pinyin: Zhège bǐ nàge guì yìdiǎnr.
examples.en: This one is a little more expensive than that one.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ bǐ tā gāo.
mistake.en: I'm taller than him.
mistake.reason: Do not use 很 in a 比 sentence; 比 already makes the comparison, so put the adjective directly after B.

title: A 有 / 没有 B (这么/那么) adj
pattern: A 有 / 没有 B (这么/那么) + adj
explanation: Use 有 to say A reaches the level of B, and 没有 to say A is not as … as B. 这么 or 那么 ("this/that much") often comes before the adjective, and the adjective is usually a positive one like 大, 高 or 贵.

examples.pinyin: nǐ dì di yǒu nǐ gāo ma
examples.en: Is your younger brother as tall as you?

examples.pinyin: jīn tiān méi yǒu zuó tiān nà me lěng
examples.en: Today is not as cold as yesterday.

examples.zh: 这个店的面包没有那个店的好吃。
examples.pinyin: zhè ge diàn de miàn bāo méi yǒu nà ge diàn de hǎo chī
examples.en: The bread at this shop is not as tasty as the bread at that shop.

mistake.pinyin: Jīntiān méiyǒu zuótiān nàme rè.
mistake.en: Today isn't as hot as yesterday.
mistake.reason: The negative of 有 is always 没有, never 不有.

title: Comparing actions
pattern: A + V 得 + 比 B + adj / A 比 B + V 得 + adj
explanation: To compare how two people do an action, put 比 B before the adjective in 'V 得 adj'. You can say it as 'A V 得比 B adj' or as 'A 比 B V 得 adj'.

examples.pinyin: wǒ pǎo de bǐ nǐ kuài
examples.en: I run faster than you.

examples.pinyin: jiějie bǐ wǒ chàng de hǎotīng
examples.en: My older sister sings better than me.

examples.pinyin: gēge shuì de bǐ wǒ wǎn
examples.en: My older brother goes to bed later than me.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ pǎo de bǐ nǐ kuài.
mistake.en: I run faster than you.
mistake.reason: 得 must come right after the verb, and 比 B goes after 得, right before the adjective.

title: 是…的
pattern: S + 是 + time/place/manner + V (+ O) + 的
explanation: Use 是…的 when a past action is already known and you want to stress when, where, how, or who did it. 是 goes before the emphasized part, and 的 goes at the end of the sentence.

examples.pinyin: wǒ shì zuò fēijī lái de
examples.en: I came by plane.

examples.pinyin: tā shì zuótiān huí jiā de
examples.en: He went home yesterday.

examples.pinyin: nǐ shì zài nǎr xué hànyǔ de
examples.en: Where did you learn Chinese?

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ shì zuótiān lái de.
mistake.en: It was yesterday that I came.
mistake.reason: In 是…的 sentences, end with 的, not 了.

title: 过 (experience)
pattern: Subj + 没 + Verb + 过 + Obj
explanation: Put 过 after a verb to say you have done something before. To say you have never done it, use 没 before the verb and keep 过: 没 + verb + 过.

examples.pinyin: wǒ qù guo zhōng guó
examples.en: I have been to China.

examples.pinyin: wǒ méi chī guo jiǎo zi
examples.en: I have never eaten dumplings.

examples.pinyin: nǐ kàn guo zhè ge diàn yǐng ma
examples.en: Have you seen this movie?

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ méi qù guo Zhōngguó.
mistake.en: I've never been to China.
mistake.reason: Do not add 了 to a 没...过 sentence, because 过 already shows past experience.

title: 着 (ongoing state)
pattern: Place + Verb + 着 + thing / Subject + Verb + 着 + thing
explanation: Put 着 after a verb to show a state or action that is continuing. For location sentences, say the place first, then verb + 着, then the thing or person there.

examples.pinyin: Ménkǒu zhàn zhe yí ge rén.
examples.en: A person is standing at the door.

examples.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang xiě zhe wǒ de míngzi.
examples.en: My name is written on the table.

examples.pinyin: Tā ná zhe shǒujī.
examples.en: He is holding a phone.

mistake.pinyin: Tā chuān zhe báisè de yīfu.
mistake.en: He's wearing white clothes.
mistake.reason: 着 shows a continuing state, so do not add 了 right after it.

title: 要 / 快要 / 就要 … 了
pattern: 快要 / 就要 / 要 + verb + 了
explanation: Put 快要, 就要 or 要 before a verb and 了 at the end to say something is about to happen. 就要 feels the soonest, and it can be used with a specific time word.

examples.pinyin: kuài yào xià yǔ le , nǐ bié chū qù 。
examples.en: It's about to rain, so don't go out.

examples.zh: 我们明天就要去中国了。
examples.pinyin: wǒ men míng tiān jiù yào qù zhōng guó le 。
examples.en: We are leaving for China tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: huǒ chē yào kāi le , kuài shàng chē !
examples.en: The train is about to leave, get on quickly!

mistake.wrong: 我们快要明天去中国了。
mistake.right: 我们明天就要去中国了。
mistake.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān jiù yào qù Zhōngguó le.
mistake.en: We're going to China tomorrow.
mistake.reason: 快要 cannot be used with a specific time word; use 就要 after the time word instead.

title: 都…了
pattern: 都 + time/state + 了
explanation: Use 都…了 to say something has 'already' reached a point, often with surprise or urgency. 都 comes before the time or state, and 了 goes at the end.

examples.pinyin: dōu shí'èr diǎn le, kuài chī fàn ba!
examples.en: It's already twelve o'clock, let's eat quickly!

examples.zh: 你都七岁了,自己洗手吧。
examples.pinyin: nǐ dōu qī suì le, zìjǐ xǐ shǒu ba.
examples.en: You're already seven years old, wash your hands yourself.

examples.pinyin: dōu wǎnshang le, tā hái méi huí jiā.
examples.en: It's already evening, and he still hasn't come home.

mistake.right: 都十二点了,你还没起床!
mistake.pinyin: Dōu shí'èr diǎn le, nǐ hái méi qǐchuáng!
mistake.en: It's already twelve o'clock and you're still not up!
mistake.reason: The 'already' meaning of 都 needs 了 at the end of the phrase.

title: Verb + 得 + adjective
pattern: S + V + O + V + 得 + adj
explanation: Use 得 after a verb to say how well or how an action is done. If the verb has an object, say the verb twice: V + O + V + 得 + adj.

examples.pinyin: Tā dǎ lánqiú dǎ de hěn hǎo.
examples.en: He plays basketball very well.

examples.pinyin: Māma zuò fàn zuò de hěn hǎochī.
examples.en: Mom cooks very tasty food.

examples.pinyin: Tā pǎo de hěn kuài.
examples.en: She runs very fast.

mistake.pinyin: Tā chàng gē chàng de hěn hǎo.
mistake.en: He sings very well.
mistake.reason: When the verb has an object, repeat the verb before 得.

title: Result complements
pattern: Verb + 错/懂/好/完/会 (result); negative: 没 + Verb + result
explanation: Add a result word right after a verb to show the outcome of the action, like 写错 (write wrongly) or 听懂 (hear and understand). To negate, use 没 before the verb: 没听懂 means you did not manage to understand.

examples.pinyin: wǒ tīng dǒng le
examples.en: I understood (what I heard).

examples.pinyin: nǐ xiě cuò le zhè ge zì
examples.en: You wrote this character wrong.

examples.pinyin: wǒ méi chī wán wǔ fàn
examples.en: I didn't finish lunch.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ méi tīng dǒng.
mistake.en: I didn't understand (what I heard).
mistake.reason: Result complements are negated with 没, not 不, because the result did not happen.

title: Direction complements (simple)
pattern: V + 来/去 ; V + 上/下/进/出/回/过 (+ 来/去)
explanation: Add 来 if the movement is toward the speaker, and 去 if it is away. Directions like 上, 下, 进, 出, 回, 过 say which way the movement goes, and 来/去 can follow them.

examples.pinyin: nǐ jìn lái ba
examples.en: Come in.

examples.pinyin: wǒ xià wǔ huí jiā qù
examples.en: I am going back home this afternoon.

examples.pinyin: tā cóng lóu shàng xià lái le
examples.en: He came down from upstairs.

mistake.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ jìnlái, wǒ zài lǐmiàn.
mistake.en: Please come in, I'm inside.
mistake.reason: The speaker is inside, so the movement is toward the speaker and needs 来, not 去.

title: Direction complements (compound)
pattern: Verb + 出来/出去/进来/进去/回来/回去/起来/上来/下去
explanation: Add a direction word after a verb to show which way the action moves. 来 means toward the speaker, 去 means away from the speaker.

examples.pinyin: tā cóng jiā lǐ pǎo chū lái le
examples.en: He ran out of the house.

examples.pinyin: qǐng jìn lái zuò ba
examples.en: Please come in and sit down.

examples.pinyin: dà jiā dōu zhàn qǐ lái le
examples.en: Everyone stood up.

mistake.wrong: 他跑进去房间了，我在房间里。
mistake.pinyin: Tā pǎo jìn fángjiān lái le.
mistake.en: He ran into the room.
mistake.reason: The speaker is inside, so use 来; a place goes between 进 and 来 (跑进房间来).

title: Verb + number of times
pattern: Subject + Verb (+过/了) + Number + 次 (+ Object)
explanation: To say how many times an action happens, put number + 次 right after the verb. If there is an object, it usually comes after 次 (for pronoun objects, it comes before).

examples.pinyin: wǒ qù guo yí cì zhōngguó
examples.en: I have been to China once.

examples.pinyin: tā yì tiān dǎ sān cì diànhuà
examples.en: He makes phone calls three times a day.

examples.pinyin: zhè ge diànyǐng wǒ kàn le liǎng cì
examples.en: I watched this movie twice.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ qù guo yí cì Zhōngguó.
mistake.en: I've been to China once.
mistake.reason: Number + 次 goes after the verb, not before it.

title: How long
pattern: S + V + 了 + duration (+ object) / A + 比 + B + adj + amount
explanation: To say how long an action lasted, put the time amount right after the verb (with 了 if completed). To say how much bigger or older, put the amount after the adjective.

examples.pinyin: wǒ xué le liǎng nián zhōngwén 。
examples.en: I studied Chinese for two years.

examples.pinyin: tā shuì le bā gè xiǎoshí 。
examples.en: He slept for eight hours.

examples.pinyin: wǒ gēge bǐ wǒ dà liǎng suì 。
examples.en: My older brother is two years older than me.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ xué le liǎng nián Zhōngwén.
mistake.en: I studied Chinese for two years.
mistake.reason: The duration goes right after the verb and before the object, not after the object.

title: Verb reduplication · 一下
pattern: V V / V 一 V / V 了 V / VV 一下 / V 一下
explanation: Repeating a verb (看看, 看一看) or adding 一下 makes an action short, light, or polite, like 'take a look' or 'have a try'. For a completed action use A了A (看了看); two-syllable verbs repeat as ABAB (休息休息).

examples.pinyin: nǐ kàn kan zhè ge
examples.en: Take a look at this.

examples.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng xiū xi xiū xi
examples.en: I want to rest a bit.

examples.pinyin: qǐng nǐ děng yí xià
examples.en: Please wait a moment.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒmen xiūxi yíxià.
mistake.en: Let's take a little rest.
mistake.reason: Use either reduplication or 一下, not both together.

title: Adjective reduplication
pattern: AA 的 / AA 地 (no 很): 个子高高的, 慢慢地说
explanation: Doubling a one-character adjective (AA) makes it more vivid. Use 的 after it to describe a noun or state, and 地 before a verb. Do not add 很 before the reduplicated form.

examples.pinyin: Tā de yǎnjing dàdà de.
examples.en: Her eyes are big and round.

examples.pinyin: Tā gèzi gāogāo de.
examples.en: He is nice and tall.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ mànmàn de shuō.
examples.en: Please speak slowly.

mistake.pinyin: Tā de yǎnjing dàdà de.
mistake.en: Her eyes are big.
mistake.reason: A reduplicated adjective is already vivid, so it doesn't take 很.

title: 别 commands
pattern: 别 + verb (+ 了)
explanation: Put 别 before a verb to say "don't do it." Add 了 at the end (别…了) to tell someone to stop something they are already doing.

examples.pinyin: bié shuō huà , lǎo shī lái le 。
examples.en: Don't talk, the teacher is here.

examples.pinyin: nǐ bié hē le , tài duō le 。
examples.en: Stop drinking, it's too much.

examples.pinyin: bié wàng le gěi mā ma dǎ diàn huà 。
examples.en: Don't forget to call Mom.

mistake.pinyin: Nǐ bié qù, wàimiàn xià yǔ le.
mistake.en: Don't go, it's raining outside.
mistake.reason: To tell someone not to do something, use 别 before the verb, not 不.

title: 还是 questions
pattern: A 还是 B?
explanation: Use 还是 between two options to ask which one someone chooses. In a statement, 或者 is used instead, but 还是 is for questions.

examples.pinyin: nǐ hē chá hái shi hē kā fēi
examples.en: Do you want tea or coffee?

examples.zh: 我们坐地铁还是坐出租车?
examples.pinyin: wǒ men zuò dì tiě hái shi zuò chū zū chē
examples.en: Shall we take the subway or a taxi?

examples.pinyin: tā shì lǎo shī hái shi xué shēng
examples.en: Is he a teacher or a student?

mistake.wrong: 你想吃面条儿或者米饭?
mistake.right: 你想吃面条儿还是米饭?
mistake.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng chī miàntiáor háishi mǐfàn?
mistake.en: Do you want noodles or rice?
mistake.reason: In a question offering a choice, use 还是, not 或者.

title: 还是…吧
pattern: 还是 + V (+ O) + 吧
explanation: Use 还是…吧 to suggest the better option after thinking about it, like 'You'd better…' or 'It's better to…'. 吧 at the end makes it a soft suggestion.

examples.zh: 你生病了,还是去看医生吧。
examples.pinyin: nǐ shēng bìng le , hái shi qù kàn yī shēng ba 。
examples.en: You're sick, you'd better go see a doctor.

examples.zh: 外面下雨了,我们还是坐出租车吧。
examples.pinyin: wài miàn xià yǔ le , wǒ men hái shi zuò chū zū chē ba 。
examples.en: It's raining outside, we'd better take a taxi.

examples.pinyin: tài wǎn le , nǐ hái shi shuì jiào ba 。
examples.en: It's too late, you'd better go to sleep.

mistake.pinyin: Nǐ háishi qù kàn yīshēng ba.
mistake.en: You'd better go see a doctor.
mistake.reason: 还是 suggesting a better choice needs 吧 at the end to sound like a suggestion.

title: 虽然…但是…
pattern: 虽然 + A, 但是 + B
explanation: Use 虽然 in the first part and 但是 in the second part to say 'Although A, B'. Unlike English, Chinese uses both words together.

examples.zh: 虽然今天很冷,但是我想去玩。
examples.pinyin: suīrán jīntiān hěn lěng, dànshì wǒ xiǎng qù wán。
examples.en: Although it's cold today, I want to go out and play.

examples.zh: 虽然这个包很贵,但是很好看。
examples.pinyin: suīrán zhège bāo hěn guì, dànshì hěn hǎokàn。
examples.en: Although this bag is expensive, it looks nice.

examples.zh: 虽然我很累,但是还要工作。
examples.pinyin: suīrán wǒ hěn lèi, dànshì hái yào gōngzuò。
examples.en: Although I'm tired, I still have to work.

mistake.wrong: 虽然今天很冷,我想去玩。
mistake.right: 虽然今天很冷,但是我想去玩。
mistake.pinyin: Suīrán jīntiān hěn lěng, dànshì wǒ xiǎng qù wán.
mistake.en: Although it's cold today, I want to go out and have fun.
mistake.reason: Chinese needs 但是 in the second part; you can't leave it out as in English.

title: 因为…所以…
pattern: 因为 + cause，所以 + result
explanation: 因为 gives the reason and 所以 gives the result. In Chinese you usually use both together, unlike English where 'because' and 'so' are not used in the same sentence.

examples.pinyin: yīnwèi xià yǔ，suǒyǐ wǒ bú qù。
examples.en: Because it's raining, I'm not going.

examples.zh: 因为他病了，所以没上班。
examples.pinyin: yīnwèi tā bìng le，suǒyǐ méi shàngbān。
examples.en: Because he is sick, he didn't go to work.

examples.zh: 因为今天很冷，所以我穿新衣服。
examples.pinyin: yīnwèi jīntiān hěn lěng，suǒyǐ wǒ chuān xīn yīfu。
examples.en: Because it's cold today, I'm wearing new clothes.

mistake.wrong: 因为我很忙，但是我不能去。
mistake.right: 因为我很忙，所以我不能去。
mistake.pinyin: Yīnwèi wǒ hěn máng, suǒyǐ wǒ bù néng qù.
mistake.en: Because I'm busy, I can't go.
mistake.reason: Use 所以 (not 但是) to introduce the result of the reason; 但是 means 'but'.

title: 一…就…
pattern: S 一 + V1, 就 + V2
explanation: Use 一…就… to say that the second action happens right after the first one, like 'as soon as' in English. Put 一 before the first verb and 就 before the second verb.

examples.zh: 我一到家就给你打电话。
examples.pinyin: wǒ yí dào jiā jiù gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà。
examples.en: As soon as I get home, I'll call you.

examples.pinyin: tā yí xiàbān jiù huí jiā。
examples.en: He goes home as soon as he gets off work.

examples.zh: 孩子一看见妈妈就笑了。
examples.pinyin: háizi yí kànjiàn māma jiù xiào le。
examples.en: The child smiled as soon as he saw Mom.

mistake.right: 我一到家就给你打电话。
mistake.pinyin: Wǒ yí dào jiā jiù gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.
mistake.en: I'll call you as soon as I get home.
mistake.reason: 一 goes before the first verb (到) and 就 must come before the second verb, not 一 again.

title: 从 · 从…到 · 往
pattern: 从 + place/time (+ 到 + place/time); 往 + direction + verb
explanation: 从 means 'from' and marks a starting point in place or time; 从 A 到 B means 'from A to B'. 往 + direction + verb means 'go toward' that direction, like 往前走 'walk forward'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóng jiā zǒu dào xuéxiào.
examples.en: I walk from home to school.

examples.zh: 我从早上八点工作到下午六点。
examples.pinyin: wǒ cóng zǎoshang bā diǎn gōngzuò dào xiàwǔ liù diǎn
examples.en: I work from eight in the morning to six in the afternoon.

examples.pinyin: qǐng wǎng qián zǒu, zài wǎng yòu zǒu
examples.en: Please walk forward, then walk right.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ cóng bā diǎn dào liù diǎn gōngzuò.
mistake.en: I work from eight to six.
mistake.reason: The 从…到… phrase goes before the verb.

title: 离 for distance
pattern: A 离 B + 很 + 远/近
explanation: Use 离 between two places to say how far apart they are. Put 很 plus 远 (far) or 近 (near) after B.

examples.pinyin: wǒ jiā lí xué xiào hěn jìn
examples.en: My home is very close to school.

examples.pinyin: jī chǎng lí zhè er hěn yuǎn
examples.en: The airport is far from here.

examples.pinyin: nǐ jiā lí dì tiě zhàn yuǎn ma
examples.en: Is your home far from the subway station?

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí gōngsī hěn jìn.
mistake.en: My home is close to the office.
mistake.reason: 离 must come before B, and the adjective 远/近 goes at the end.

title: 给 · 送给
pattern: 给 + person + verb; verb + 给 + person + thing
explanation: Use 给 before a person and a verb to say you do something for or to that person. Use a verb like 送 or 卖 followed by 给 and then the person and the thing to say who receives something.

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.en: Call me tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ sòng gěi tā yì běn shū.
examples.en: I give her a book as a gift.

examples.pinyin: Māma gěi wǒ zuò fàn.
examples.en: Mom cooks for me.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān gěi tā dǎ diànhuà.
mistake.en: I'll call her tomorrow.
mistake.reason: Put 给 + person before the verb, and put the time word before 给.

title: 跟
pattern: A 跟 B + verb / A 跟 B 一起 + verb / A 跟 B + 都 + ...
explanation: 跟 + person + verb means 'do something with someone'. 跟 can also join two nouns like 'and', but it is more common in speech with 和.

examples.pinyin: wǒ gēn péng you qù kàn diàn yǐng
examples.en: I'm going to see a movie with a friend.

examples.pinyin: tā gēn wǒ yì qǐ chī wǔ fàn
examples.en: He eats lunch with me.

examples.pinyin: gē ge gēn jiě jie dōu zài zhōng guó
examples.en: My older brother and older sister are both in China.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ gēn māma qù shāngdiàn.
mistake.en: I'm going to the store with my mom.
mistake.reason: The 跟 phrase must come before the verb, not after it.

title: 请 / 叫 / 让 + person + verb
pattern: A + 请/叫/让 + B + verb
explanation: Use 请 to politely invite or ask someone to do something. Use 叫 or 让 to tell, make or let someone do something. The person goes right after 请/叫/让 and before the verb.

examples.pinyin: yī shēng ràng wǒ duō xiū xi
examples.en: The doctor told me to rest more.

examples.pinyin: mā ma jiào wǒ zǎo diǎn shuì jiào
examples.en: Mom told me to go to bed a bit earlier.

examples.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng qǐng nǐ hē chá
examples.en: I would like to invite you to have tea.

mistake.pinyin: Yīshēng ràng wǒ xiūxi.
mistake.en: The doctor told me to rest.
mistake.reason: The person must come right after 让 and before the verb.

title: 可能
pattern: S + 可能 + (不) + Verb
explanation: 可能 goes before the verb to say something might happen or might be true. To say 'might not', put 不 after 可能: 可能不 + verb.

examples.pinyin: Tā kěnéng bù lái le.
examples.en: He might not come anymore.

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān kěnéng xià yǔ.
examples.en: It might rain tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Māma xiànzài kěnéng zài chāoshì.
examples.en: Mom might be at the supermarket now.

mistake.pinyin: Tā kěnéng bù lái le.
mistake.en: He might not come anymore.
mistake.reason: To say 'might not', use 可能不 + verb; 不可能 means 'impossible', which is much stronger.

title: 再 and 就
pattern: S + 再 + V (again, later) / S + 就 + V (right away, as early as, just)
explanation: 再 means doing something again or later in the future, and also 'then' after a condition. 就 means something happens right away, earlier than expected, or 'just/only'.

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān zài lái ba.
examples.en: Come again tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ liù diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
examples.en: I got up as early as six o'clock.

examples.pinyin: Chī le fàn zài qù shāngdiàn.
examples.en: Eat first, then go to the store.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zài hē yì bēi chá.
mistake.en: I'd like another cup of tea.
mistake.reason: 再 goes right before the verb it modifies.

title: 还 · 已经 · 快
pattern: 还 + V/adj (still); 已经 + V + 了 (already); 快 + V + 了 (soon); 有时候 / 经常 + V (sometimes / often)
explanation: 还 means 'still', 已经…了 means 'already', and 快…了 means 'soon'. 有时候 (sometimes) and 经常 (often) go before the verb to say how often something happens.

examples.pinyin: Tā hái zài shuìjiào.
examples.en: He is still sleeping.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng chī fàn le.
examples.en: I have already eaten.

examples.pinyin: Huǒchē kuài dào le.
examples.en: The train will arrive soon.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ yǐjīng chī fàn le.
mistake.en: I've already eaten.
mistake.reason: 已经 normally needs 了 at the end of the sentence to show the action is already done.

title: 这么 · 那么 · 这样 · 那样
pattern: 这么/那么 + adj/verb;  这样/那样 + verb/adj
explanation: 这么 means 'so/this way' for something near, and 那么 means 'so/that way' for something far or already mentioned. They go before adjectives or verbs. 这样 and 那样 mean 'like this' and 'like that'.

examples.pinyin: jīn tiān zhè me lěng!
examples.en: It's so cold today!

examples.pinyin: nǐ wèi shén me nà me máng?
examples.en: Why are you so busy?

examples.pinyin: zhè ge zì zhè yàng xiě.
examples.en: This character is written like this.

mistake.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì zhème lěng.
mistake.en: The weather is so cold today.
mistake.reason: 这么 already means 'so', so do not add 很 before the adjective.

title: Adjective + 地 + verb
pattern: Adj + 地 + Verb
explanation: Put 地 after an adjective to describe how an action is done, like -ly in English. Use 的 before nouns and 得 after verbs to describe the result or degree.

examples.pinyin: háizi men kuàilè de wán。
examples.en: The children play happily.

examples.pinyin: tā gāoxìng de shuō: xièxie!
examples.en: He said happily: Thanks!

examples.pinyin: nǐ màn màn de zǒu。
examples.en: You walk slowly.

mistake.pinyin: Tā gāoxìng de shuōhuà.
mistake.en: He spoke happily.
mistake.reason: Use 地, not 的, between an adjective and the verb it describes.

title: Topic first
pattern: Topic + Subject + Verb/Comment (object or topic placed first)
explanation: In Chinese you can put the thing you are talking about at the front, then add a comment about it. The topic can be an object (饭吃了) or a person with a description (他身体很好).

examples.pinyin: zhè běn shū wǒ kàn wán le
examples.en: I finished reading this book.

examples.pinyin: tā shēntǐ hěn hǎo
examples.en: His health is very good.

examples.pinyin: wǎnfàn wǒ zuò hǎo le
examples.en: I have made dinner.

mistake.pinyin: Zhè běn shū wǒ kàn wán le.
mistake.en: I've finished reading this book.
mistake.reason: When the object is the topic at the front, don't repeat it after the verb.

title: Approximate numbers
pattern: 几 + MW / Number + 多 + MW / Number + MW + 多 + noun
explanation: 几 asks about or means a small number (under ten). 多 after a number means 'a bit more than': after a round number like 二十 it comes before the measure word (二十多个), but after a single-digit number plus measure word it follows it (一个多小时).

examples.pinyin: nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ kǒu rén
examples.en: How many people are in your family?

examples.zh: 我们班有二十多个学生。
examples.pinyin: wǒ men bān yǒu èr shí duō gè xué shēng
examples.en: Our class has twenty-some students.

examples.pinyin: wǒ děng le yí gè duō xiǎo shí
examples.en: I waited more than an hour.

mistake.wrong: 我们班有二十个多学生。
mistake.right: 我们班有二十多个学生。
mistake.pinyin: Wǒmen bān yǒu èrshí duō ge xuésheng.
mistake.en: There are more than twenty students in our class.
mistake.reason: After a round number like 二十, 多 goes before the measure word, not after it.

title: …什么的
pattern: A、B、C 什么的
explanation: Put 什么的 after a short list of things to mean 'and so on' or 'and stuff like that'. It makes the list open-ended, and you usually list two or three items first.

examples.zh: 我喜欢吃苹果、面包什么的。
examples.pinyin: wǒ xǐhuan chī píngguǒ、miànbāo shénmede。
examples.en: I like eating apples, bread, and so on.

examples.pinyin: tā jiā yǒu māo、gǒu shénmede。
examples.en: His family has cats, dogs, and the like.

examples.zh: 我想去超市买牛奶、鸡蛋什么的。
examples.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng qù chāoshì mǎi niúnǎi、jīdàn shénmede。
examples.en: I want to go to the supermarket to buy milk, eggs, and so on.

mistake.wrong: 我喜欢吃苹果什么的、面包。
mistake.right: 我喜欢吃苹果、面包什么的。
mistake.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan chī píngguǒ, miànbāo shénmede.
mistake.en: I like eating apples, bread and so on.
mistake.reason: 什么的 must come at the end of the whole list, not in the middle.

title: 把 + object + verb + 在/到 + place
pattern: S + 把 + object + verb + 在/到 + place
explanation: Use 把 to say what you do to a specific thing, and where it ends up. The verb must be followed by 在 or 到 plus the place, never alone.

examples.pinyin: wǒ bǎ shū fàng zài zhuōzi shang
examples.en: I put the book on the table.

examples.pinyin: tā bǎ chē kāi dào xuéxiào le
examples.en: He drove the car to school.

examples.zh: 请你把手机放在椅子上。
examples.pinyin: qǐng nǐ bǎ shǒujī fàng zài yǐzi shang
examples.en: Please put the phone on the chair.

mistake.pinyin: wǒ bǎ shū fàng zài zhuōzi shang
mistake.en: I put the book on the table.
mistake.reason: 把 and its object must come before the verb, not after it.

title: 把 + object + verb (+ 给) + person
pattern: S + 把 + thing + verb + 给 + person
explanation: Use 把 to put the thing first, then a verb of handing over (还, 送, etc.) plus 给 and the receiver. It stresses what happens to the thing: it ends up with that person.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè běn shū gěi tā.
examples.en: Please give this book to him.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān bǎ qián huán gěi nǐ.
examples.en: I'll give the money back to you tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ lǐwù sòng gěi nǚpéngyou.
examples.en: She gives the gift to her girlfriend.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ qián huán gěi péngyou.
mistake.en: I give the money back to my friend.
mistake.reason: After a verb like 还 or 送, you need 给 before the receiver.

title: 把 + object + verb + complement
pattern: S + 把 + object + verb + complement (result/direction/state)
explanation: Use 把 to move the object before the verb and say what happens to it. The verb must be followed by something, like 完, 上, 进去 or 得 + state, and 没 goes before 把.

examples.pinyin: wǒ bǎ zuòyè xiě wán le
examples.en: I finished writing my homework.

examples.pinyin: qǐng nǐ bǎ mén guān shang
examples.en: Please close the door.

examples.zh: 妈妈把衣服洗得很干净。
examples.pinyin: māma bǎ yīfu xǐ de hěn gānjìng
examples.en: Mom washed the clothes very clean.

mistake.pinyin: wǒ méi bǎ zuòyè xiě wán
mistake.en: I haven't finished my homework.
mistake.reason: Negation 没 goes before 把, not after it.

title: 被 passive
pattern: A + 被 (+ doer) + verb + other element (了 / 走 / 完)
explanation: 被 makes the thing affected the subject, and the doer comes after 被 (it can be left out). The verb needs something after it, like 了 or 走, and the event is usually unwelcome.

examples.pinyin: wǒ de shǒujī bèi tā ná zǒu le
examples.en: My phone was taken away by him.

examples.pinyin: wǒ de qián bèi dìdi huā le
examples.en: My money was spent by my younger brother.

examples.pinyin: wǒ de shū bèi péngyou jiè zǒu le
examples.en: My book was borrowed by a friend.

mistake.pinyin: wǒ de shǒujī méi bèi tā ná zǒu
mistake.en: My phone wasn't taken away by him.
mistake.reason: Put 没 before 被, not between 被 and the verb.

title: Potential complements: 得 / 不
pattern: Verb + 得/不 + complement (听得懂 / 看不见)
explanation: Put 得 (can) or 不 (can't) between a verb and its result or direction complement to say whether something is possible. For a yes/no question, use the 得 and 不 forms together, like 听得懂听不懂.

examples.pinyin: nǐ shuō de tài kuài, wǒ tīng bu dǒng。
examples.en: You speak too fast, I can't understand.

examples.pinyin: zhè me duō jiǎo zi, wǒ chī bu wán。
examples.en: There are so many dumplings, I can't finish them.

examples.pinyin: nǐ kàn de jiàn hēi bǎn ma?
examples.en: Can you see the blackboard?

mistake.pinyin: zhè ge zì wǒ tīng bu dǒng。
mistake.en: I can't understand this word.
mistake.reason: Use the potential form 听不懂 instead of 不能 plus a result complement.

title: Result complements 到 / 住 / 走 / 上
pattern: V + 到/住/走/上 (result complement)
explanation: A result complement after a verb shows the outcome of the action: 到 means reaching the goal, 住 means fixed in place, 走 means away, and 上 means closed or attached.

examples.pinyin: wǒ zhǎo dào shǒu jī le
examples.en: I found my phone.

examples.pinyin: qǐng jì zhù zhè ge zì
examples.en: Please remember this character.

examples.pinyin: tā kāi zǒu le wǒ de chē
examples.en: He drove my car away.

mistake.pinyin: qǐng guān shàng mén
mistake.en: Please close the door.
mistake.reason: Without the complement 上, 关 only names the action, not the result of the door being closed.

title: Extended directional complements
pattern: V + 起来 / 下来 / 下去 / 出来 / 上 (figurative)
explanation: Directional words after a verb can show abstract meanings: 想出 means to think of something, 爱上 means to fall in love with, 起来 means to start, 下去 means to continue, and 下来 means to settle or stay.

examples.pinyin: dà jiā dōu xiào qǐ lái le 。
examples.en: Everyone started laughing.

examples.pinyin: nǐ shuō xià qù ba 。
examples.en: Go on talking.

examples.zh: 他爱上了一个中国女孩儿。
examples.pinyin: tā ài shàng le yí gè zhōng guó nǚ hái ér 。
examples.en: He fell in love with a Chinese girl.

mistake.pinyin: tiān qì lěng le ,xià qǐ yǔ lái le 。
mistake.en: The weather got cold, and it started to rain.
mistake.reason: When the verb has an object, split 起来 around it: 下起雨来, not 下雨起来.

title: Degree: 得很 / 极了 / 坏了
pattern: Adj + 得很 / Adj + 极了 / Adj/Verb + 坏了
explanation: Put 得很 or 极了 after an adjective to mean 'extremely', as in 好得很 or 好极了. Use 坏了 after an adjective or verb for an extreme, unpleasant state like 累坏了 or 饿坏了.

examples.pinyin: zhè lǐ de dōng xi guì de hěn
examples.en: Things here are extremely expensive.

examples.pinyin: jīn tiān tiān qì hǎo jí le
examples.en: The weather today is fantastic!

examples.pinyin: wǒ jīn tiān lèi huài le
examples.en: I'm exhausted today.

mistake.pinyin: jīn tiān rè de hěn
mistake.en: It's extremely hot today.
mistake.reason: 得很 already means 'very', so don't add 很 before the adjective.

title: Time since something happened
pattern: Subject + Verb (+ Object) + time + 了
explanation: Put the time length after the verb (and object) and end with 了 to say how long it has been since the action happened or ended. It means 'it has been X time since...'.

examples.pinyin: tā lái běi jīng sān nián le
examples.en: It has been three years since he came to Beijing.

examples.pinyin: wǒ chū guó liǎng nián le
examples.en: It has been two years since I went abroad.

examples.pinyin: tā zǒu le shí fēn zhōng le
examples.en: It has been ten minutes since he left.

mistake.pinyin: wǒ chū guó liǎng nián le
mistake.en: It has been two years since I went abroad.
mistake.reason: The time length goes after the verb and object, not before the verb as in English.

title: A 比 B 更 / 还 + adjective
pattern: A 比 B 更/还 + adj
explanation: Use 比 to compare A and B, then add 更 or 还 before the adjective to say A is even more so. Never use 很 or 非常 in a 比 sentence.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān gèng lěng.
examples.en: Today is even colder than yesterday.

examples.pinyin: Tā bǐ wǒ hái gāo.
examples.en: He is even taller than me.

examples.pinyin: Zhège bǐ nàge gèng hǎochī.
examples.en: This one is even tastier than that one.

mistake.pinyin: Jīntiān bǐ zuótiān gèng lěng.
mistake.en: Today is even colder than yesterday.
mistake.reason: In a 比 sentence use 更 or 还, never 很 or 非常, before the adjective.

title: A 跟 B 一样 (+ adjective)
pattern: A 跟 B 一样 (+ adj)
explanation: Use 跟 to link two things and 一样 to say they are the same. Add an adjective after 一样 to say how they are the same; for different, use 不一样.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shū gēn nǐ de yíyàng.
examples.en: My book is the same as yours.

examples.pinyin: Tā gēn tā gēge yíyàng gāo.
examples.en: He is as tall as his older brother.

examples.zh: 这个电脑跟那个不一样。
examples.pinyin: Zhège diànnǎo gēn nàge bù yíyàng.
examples.en: This computer is not the same as that one.

mistake.pinyin: Tā gēn tā gēge yíyàng gāo.
mistake.en: He is as tall as his older brother.
mistake.reason: Put 跟 + B before 一样, and the adjective comes after 一样.

title: A 不比 B + adjective
pattern: A 不比 B + adj
explanation: 不比 means 'A is not more [adj] than B'. A is about the same as B or even less, so it is often used to disagree with someone. It is different from 没有…那么, which clearly says A is less than B.

examples.pinyin: wǒ bù bǐ tā gāo
examples.en: I'm not taller than him.

examples.zh: 这里的东西不比那里贵。
examples.pinyin: zhè lǐ de dōng xi bù bǐ nà lǐ guì
examples.en: The things here are not more expensive than there.

examples.pinyin: jīn tiān bù bǐ zuó tiān lěng
examples.en: Today is not colder than yesterday.

mistake.pinyin: wǒ bù bǐ tā gāo
mistake.en: I'm not taller than him.
mistake.reason: Do not put 很 or other degree words before the adjective in a 比 sentence.

title: A 比 B 早 / 晚 / 多 / 少 + verb + amount
pattern: A 比 B + 早/晚/多/少 + verb + amount
explanation: Put 早, 晚, 多 or 少 right after 比 B, then the verb, then the amount, to say how much more, less, earlier or later someone did something. The amount comes last.

examples.pinyin: wǒ bǐ tā zǎo lái shí fēn zhōng
examples.en: I came ten minutes earlier than him.

examples.pinyin: tā bǐ wǒ duō mǎi le liǎng běn shū
examples.en: He bought two more books than I did.

examples.zh: 今天比昨天少花了五十块。
examples.pinyin: jīn tiān bǐ zuó tiān shǎo huā le wǔ shí kuài
examples.en: Today I spent fifty yuan less than yesterday.

mistake.pinyin: wǒ bǐ tā zǎo lái shí fēn zhōng
mistake.en: I came ten minutes earlier than him.
mistake.reason: Put 早 before the verb (早来), not after it, and keep the amount at the end.

title: Appearing and disappearing
pattern: Place + V + 来/走 + 了 + Number + MW + Noun
explanation: Use this pattern to say that someone or something appeared (来) or disappeared (走, 少) at a place. The place comes first, and the new or missing thing comes last with a number and measure word.

examples.pinyin: Qiánmiàn zǒu lái le yí ge rén.
examples.en: A person walked up ahead.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lái le yí wèi kèrén.
examples.en: A guest has come to my home.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bān zǒu le liǎng ge tóngxué.
examples.en: Two classmates left our class.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lái le yí ge rén.
mistake.en: A person has come to my home.
mistake.reason: Put the place first and the newly appearing person after the verb, not before it.

title: 是……的 for the speaker's view
pattern: S + 是 + adj / verb phrase + 的
explanation: Put 是 before an adjective or verb phrase and 的 at the end to state your opinion or judgment firmly, as if saying 'I'm sure of it'. It sounds more certain than a plain statement.

examples.pinyin: zhè ge bàn fǎ shì hěn hǎo de 。
examples.en: This method is very good (I'm sure).

examples.pinyin: tā shì bú huì lái de 。
examples.en: He definitely won't come.

examples.pinyin: wǒ shì tóng yì de 。
examples.en: I do agree.

mistake.pinyin: tā shì bú huì lái de 。
mistake.en: He definitely won't come.
mistake.reason: The 是……的 pattern needs the closing 的 at the end; without it the sentence is incomplete.

title: Repeating the verb
pattern: Subj + V + Obj + V + 得/了 + complement
explanation: When a verb has both an object and a complement (like degree or duration), repeat the verb after the object. The first verb takes the object, and the second verb takes 得 or 了 and the complement.

examples.pinyin: Tā shuō Hànyǔ shuō de hěn hǎo.
examples.en: He speaks Chinese very well.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ děng nǐ děng le yí gè xiǎoshí.
examples.en: I waited for you for an hour.

examples.pinyin: Māma zuò fàn zuò de hěn hǎochī.
examples.en: Mom cooks very deliciously.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ xiě Hànzì xiě de hěn hǎo.
mistake.en: I write Chinese characters very well.
mistake.reason: You must repeat the verb after the object before 得; 得 cannot follow the object directly.

title: Verb 1 + 着 + verb 2
pattern: Verb 1 + 着 + Verb 2
explanation: 着 after the first verb shows the way or state in which the second action happens. Verb 1 is the manner (like smiling or standing) while verb 2 is the main action.

examples.pinyin: tā xiào zhe shuō huà
examples.en: She talks while smiling.

examples.pinyin: wǒ men zǒu zhe qù xué xiào ba
examples.en: Let's walk to school.

examples.pinyin: tā xǐ huan zhàn zhe chī fàn
examples.en: He likes to eat standing up.

mistake.pinyin: tā zuò zhe kàn diàn shì
mistake.en: He watches TV sitting down.
mistake.reason: Use 着, not 了, after the first verb to show the manner in which the second action is done.

title: 不是……吗? for emphasis
pattern: A 不是 + V/phrase + 吗？
explanation: Use 不是……吗 to ask a rhetorical question that means 'surely' or 'isn't it the case that'. You already believe the answer is yes, and you use it to remind or gently challenge the listener.

examples.pinyin: nǐ bú shì huì shuō hàn yǔ ma
examples.en: You speak Chinese, don't you?

examples.pinyin: zhè bú shì nǐ de shū ma
examples.en: Isn't this your book?

examples.pinyin: nǐ bú shì míng tiān shàng bān ma
examples.en: Don't you work tomorrow?

mistake.pinyin: nǐ bú shì huì shuō hàn yǔ ma
mistake.en: You speak Chinese, don't you?
mistake.reason: For 'surely', put 不是 before the whole phrase; 不会……吗 just asks a plain question about ability.

title: 怎样 + verb
pattern: 怎样 + Verb
explanation: 怎样 means 'how' and is a bit more formal than 怎么. Put it right before a verb to ask in what way something is done.

examples.pinyin: zhè ge zì zěn yàng xiě ?
examples.en: How do you write this character?

examples.pinyin: nǐ shì zěn yàng xué hàn yǔ de ?
examples.en: How did you learn Chinese?

examples.pinyin: qù jī chǎng zěn yàng zǒu ?
examples.en: How do I get to the airport?

mistake.pinyin: zhè ge zì zěn yàng xiě ?
mistake.en: How do you write this character?
mistake.reason: 怎样 must come before the verb, not after it.

title: Question words meaning 'any' or 'some'
pattern: 疑问词 + 都/也 + (不/没) + V;  疑问词…就…疑问词;  V + 点儿 + 疑问词
explanation: A question word with 都 or 也 means 'any-' (everything, anyone, anywhere). Repeating the same question word links two parts (想吃什么就吃什么, 'eat whatever you want'), and 什么/哪儿 after a verb can mean 'something/somewhere'.

examples.pinyin: wǒ shén me dōu bù xiǎng chī。
examples.en: I don't want to eat anything.

examples.pinyin: jīn tiān wǒ nǎr yě méi qù。
examples.en: I didn't go anywhere today.

examples.pinyin: nǐ xiǎng chī shén me jiù chī shén me。
examples.en: Eat whatever you want.

mistake.pinyin: wǒ shén me dōu bù xiǎng chī。
mistake.en: I don't want to eat anything.
mistake.reason: To say 'not anything', put 什么 before 都 and the verb, rather than leaving it after the verb as in a plain question.

title: 先……，再 / 然后……
pattern: 先 + V1，再/然后 + V2
explanation: Use 先 before the first action and 再 or 然后 before the second to say what happens in order. 再 usually sits right before the second verb, while 然后 means 'and then' and starts the next part.

examples.pinyin: wǒ men xiān chī fàn , zài huí jiā 。
examples.en: We'll eat first, then go home.

examples.pinyin: xiān qù chāo shì , rán hòu huí jiā 。
examples.en: First go to the supermarket, then go home.

examples.pinyin: nǐ xiān xǐ shǒu , zài hē chá ba 。
examples.en: Wash your hands first, then drink tea.

mistake.pinyin: wǒ xiān chī fàn , zài qù shàng bān 。
mistake.en: I'll eat first, then go to work.
mistake.reason: 再 must come directly before the second verb, not before the subject.

title: 或者……或者…… / 或
pattern: 或者 A，或者 B / A 或者 B（都可以）
explanation: Use 或者 to say "either A or B" in statements, when you give options or say you are fine with either. In questions ("A or B?") use 还是 instead.

examples.zh: 我们或者今天去，或者明天去。
examples.pinyin: wǒ men huò zhě jīn tiān qù ， huò zhě míng tiān qù 。
examples.en: We will go either today or tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: hē chá huò zhě kā fēi dōu kě yǐ 。
examples.en: Tea or coffee, either is fine.

examples.zh: 你可以坐地铁或者坐出租车。
examples.pinyin: nǐ kě yǐ zuò dì tiě huò zhě zuò chū zū chē 。
examples.en: You can take the subway or a taxi.

mistake.pinyin: nǐ hē chá hái shi kā fēi ？
mistake.en: Do you drink tea or coffee?
mistake.reason: In a question offering a choice, use 还是, not 或者.

title: 一会儿……，一会儿……
pattern: S + 一会儿 + A，一会儿 + B
explanation: Use 一会儿……，一会儿…… to say that something keeps switching between two states or actions. Put a verb or adjective after each 一会儿.

examples.zh: 天气一会儿冷，一会儿热。
examples.pinyin: tiān qì yí huìr lěng, yí huìr rè.
examples.en: The weather is cold one minute and hot the next.

examples.zh: 他一会儿看书，一会儿看电视。
examples.pinyin: tā yí huìr kàn shū, yí huìr kàn diàn shì.
examples.en: He reads for a while, then watches TV for a while.

examples.zh: 孩子一会儿哭，一会儿笑。
examples.pinyin: hái zi yí huìr kū, yí huìr xiào.
examples.en: The child cries one moment and laughs the next.

mistake.wrong: 他一会儿看书，也看电视。
mistake.right: 他一会儿看书，一会儿看电视。
mistake.pinyin: tā yí huìr kàn shū, yí huìr kàn diàn shì.
mistake.en: He reads for a while, then watches TV for a while.
mistake.reason: The second part needs its own 一会儿 to show the alternation; 也 does not work here.

title: 又……又……
pattern: S + 又 + adj/verb phrase 1 + 又 + adj/verb phrase 2
explanation: Use 又……又…… to say that someone or something has two qualities, or does two things, at the same time. Both parts should be the same kind of word, such as two adjectives or two verb phrases.

examples.pinyin: zhè ge píng guǒ yòu dà yòu hǎo chī
examples.en: This apple is big and delicious.

examples.pinyin: tā yòu huì chàng gē yòu huì tiào wǔ
examples.en: She can both sing and dance.

examples.pinyin: jīn tiān tiān qì yòu lěng yòu xià yǔ
examples.en: Today the weather is both cold and rainy.

mistake.wrong: 这个手机又很贵又很大。
mistake.pinyin: zhè ge shǒu jī yòu guì yòu dà
mistake.en: This phone is both expensive and big.
mistake.reason: Do not add 很 after 又; put the adjective directly after each 又.

title: 一边……，一边……
pattern: S + 一边 + V1 (+O)，一边 + V2 (+O)
explanation: Use 一边……，一边…… to say someone does two actions at the same time. Put 一边 before each verb; in short form you can say 边V1边V2.

examples.zh: 他一边吃饭，一边看手机。
examples.pinyin: Tā yìbiān chī fàn, yìbiān kàn shǒujī.
examples.en: He looks at his phone while eating.

examples.zh: 我们一边走路，一边说话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yìbiān zǒulù, yìbiān shuōhuà.
examples.en: We talk while walking.

examples.zh: 妈妈一边做饭，一边听歌。
examples.pinyin: Māma yìbiān zuò fàn, yìbiān tīng gē.
examples.en: Mom listens to songs while cooking.

mistake.right: 他一边喝茶，一边看电视。
mistake.pinyin: Tā yìbiān hē chá, yìbiān kàn diànshì.
mistake.en: He watches TV while drinking tea.
mistake.reason: You need 一边 before both actions, not just the first one.

title: 不但……，而且……
pattern: S + 不但 + A，(S) 而且 + B
explanation: Use 不但……，而且…… to say 'not only A but also B'. If both clauses share the same subject, put the subject before 不但 and don't repeat it before 而且.

examples.zh: 他不但会说汉语，而且说得很好。
examples.pinyin: Tā búdàn huì shuō Hànyǔ, érqiě shuō de hěn hǎo.
examples.en: He can not only speak Chinese, but also speaks it very well.

examples.zh: 这个店的东西不但好吃，而且很便宜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge diàn de dōngxi búdàn hǎochī, érqiě hěn piányi.
examples.en: The food at this shop is not only tasty, but also cheap.

examples.zh: 我妈妈不但会做饭，而且很喜欢做饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ māma búdàn huì zuò fàn, érqiě hěn xǐhuan zuò fàn.
examples.en: My mom can not only cook, but also loves cooking.

mistake.wrong: 不但他会说汉语，而且说得很好。
mistake.right: 他不但会说汉语，而且说得很好。
mistake.pinyin: Tā búdàn huì shuō Hànyǔ, érqiě shuō de hěn hǎo.
mistake.en: He can not only speak Chinese, but also speaks it very well.
mistake.reason: When both clauses share a subject, put it before 不但, not after.

title: 虽然……，可是 / 可……
pattern: 虽然 + A，可是 / 可 + B
explanation: 虽然 introduces a fact, and 可是 or 可 introduces the contrast, like 'although... but...'. In Chinese you use both words together, and 可 can also stand alone to mean 'but'.

examples.pinyin: Suīrán hěn lèi, kěshì hěn gāoxìng.
examples.en: Although I'm tired, I'm very happy.

examples.zh: 虽然东西很贵，可是很好看。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán dōngxi hěn guì, kěshì hěn hǎokàn.
examples.en: Although the thing is expensive, it looks nice.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù, kě méi shíjiān.
examples.en: I want to go, but I have no time.

mistake.wrong: 虽然今天很冷，我很想去玩儿。
mistake.right: 虽然今天很冷，可是我很想去玩儿。
mistake.pinyin: Suīrán jīntiān hěn lěng, kěshì wǒ hěn xiǎng qù wánr.
mistake.en: Although it's cold today, I really want to go out and play.
mistake.reason: Chinese needs 可是 or 可 in the second clause; 虽然 alone is not enough.

title: 如果……(的话)，就……
pattern: 如果 + condition (的话)，(subject) 就 + result
explanation: Use 如果 to say 'if' and 就 before the verb in the result clause. You can add 的话 after the condition, and you may drop 如果 and keep only 的话.

examples.zh: 如果明天下雨，我们就不去了。
examples.pinyin: rú guǒ míng tiān xià yǔ , wǒ men jiù bù qù le 。
examples.en: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.

examples.pinyin: yǒu shí jiān de huà , jiù lái ba 。
examples.en: If you have time, then come.

examples.zh: 如果你累了的话，就休息一下。
examples.pinyin: rú guǒ nǐ lèi le de huà , jiù xiū xi yí xià 。
examples.en: If you're tired, then take a rest.

mistake.wrong: 如果明天下雨，我们不去了。
mistake.right: 如果明天下雨，我们就不去了。
mistake.pinyin: rú guǒ míng tiān xià yǔ , wǒ men jiù bù qù le 。
mistake.en: If it rains tomorrow, we won't go.
mistake.reason: The result clause normally needs 就 before the verb to link it to the condition.

title: 只有……，才……
pattern: 只有 + condition，才 + result
explanation: 只有……，才…… means 'only if X, then Y': X is the one and only condition. Compare 只要……就……, where X is a sufficient condition and other ways may also work.

examples.zh: 只有多练习，才能说好汉语。
examples.pinyin: zhǐ yǒu duō liàn xí， cái néng shuō hǎo hàn yǔ。
examples.en: Only by practicing a lot can you speak Chinese well.

examples.pinyin: zhǐ yǒu nǐ qù， tā cái gāo xìng。
examples.en: He'll be happy only if you go.

examples.zh: 只有早点儿起床，才不会迟到。
examples.pinyin: zhǐ yǒu zǎo diǎnr qǐ chuáng， cái bú huì chí dào。
examples.en: Only if you get up early won't you be late.

mistake.wrong: 只有多练习，就能说好汉语。
mistake.right: 只有多练习，才能说好汉语。
mistake.pinyin: zhǐ yǒu duō liàn xí， cái néng shuō hǎo hàn yǔ。
mistake.en: Only by practicing a lot can you speak Chinese well.
mistake.reason: 只有 pairs with 才, not 就; 就 belongs with 只要 (e.g. 只要多练习，就能说好).

title: 只要……，就……
pattern: 只要 + condition，（主语）就 + result
explanation: 只要 introduces a condition that is enough to make the result happen. 就 goes before the verb in the second clause and links the result to that condition.

examples.zh: 只要你努力，就能学好汉语。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyào nǐ nǔlì, jiù néng xué hǎo Hànyǔ.
examples.en: As long as you work hard, you can learn Chinese well.

examples.zh: 只要有时间，我就去看你。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyào yǒu shíjiān, wǒ jiù qù kàn nǐ.
examples.en: As long as I have time, I'll come see you.

examples.zh: 只要不下雨，我们就去公园。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐyào bú xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù qù gōngyuán.
examples.en: As long as it doesn't rain, we'll go to the park.

mistake.pinyin: Zhǐyào nǐ lái, wǒ jiù gāoxìng.
mistake.en: As long as you come, I'll be happy.
mistake.reason: Learners often forget 就 in the second clause; it is needed to complete the pattern.

title: 为了 / 为
pattern: 为了 + goal，subject + action；为 + person + verb
explanation: 为了 introduces a purpose or goal, followed by the action taken to reach it. 为 + person means 'for (someone)', and 为什么 means 'why'.

examples.zh: 为了学好汉语，我每天练习。
examples.pinyin: wèi le xué hǎo hàn yǔ，wǒ měi tiān liàn xí。
examples.en: In order to learn Chinese well, I practice every day.

examples.zh: 妈妈为我做了一个蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: mā ma wèi wǒ zuò le yí gè dàn gāo。
examples.en: Mom made a cake for me.

examples.pinyin: nǐ wèi shén me bú qù shàng bān？
examples.en: Why aren't you going to work?

mistake.wrong: 我每天练习，为了学好汉语。
mistake.right: 为了学好汉语，我每天练习。
mistake.pinyin: wèi le xué hǎo hàn yǔ，wǒ měi tiān liàn xí。
mistake.en: In order to learn Chinese well, I practice every day.
mistake.reason: In Chinese the 为了 goal usually comes first, before the action, not after it like English 'in order to'.

title: Verb 1 + 了 + … 就 + verb 2
pattern: Verb 1 + 了 + (object) + 就 + Verb 2
explanation: Use this to say that as soon as the first action is finished, the second action follows right away. 了 goes after the first verb, and 就 comes before the second verb.

examples.pinyin: wǒ xià le kè jiù qù zhǎo nǐ
examples.en: As soon as I finish class, I'll go find you.

examples.pinyin: tā chī le fàn jiù zǒu le
examples.en: He left as soon as he finished eating.

examples.pinyin: wǒ men xià le bān jiù huí jiā
examples.en: We go home as soon as we get off work.

mistake.pinyin: wǒ chī le fàn jiù qù xué xiào
mistake.en: I go to school as soon as I finish eating.
mistake.reason: Put 了 right after the first verb (吃了饭), not at the end of the first clause.

title: 除了……(以外)，……还 / 也 / 都……
pattern: 除了 A (以外)，S 还/也 + V (besides A) ; 除了 A (以外)，S 都 + V (except A)
explanation: Use 除了 with 还 or 也 to say "besides A, there is more". Use 除了 with 都 to say "everyone except A".

examples.zh: 除了汉语，他还会说中文。
examples.pinyin: chúle hànyǔ, tā hái huì shuō zhōngwén.
examples.en: Besides Chinese, he can also speak Mandarin.

examples.zh: 除了苹果，我也喜欢吃面包。
examples.pinyin: chúle píngguǒ, wǒ yě xǐhuan chī miànbāo.
examples.en: Besides apples, I also like eating bread.

examples.pinyin: chúle tā, wǒmen dōu qù le.
examples.en: Except him, we all went.

mistake.wrong: 除了我哥哥，我们都去了，我也去了。
mistake.right: 除了我哥哥以外，我们都去了。
mistake.pinyin: chúle wǒ gēge yǐwài, wǒmen dōu qù le.
mistake.en: Except my older brother, we all went.
mistake.reason: For "except", use 除了 with 都 and don't add 也 or 还, which would mean "besides".

title: 对……来说 / 在……看来 / 看来 / 一般来说
pattern: 对 + 人 + 来说 / 在 + 人 + 看来 / 看来 + 判断 / 一般来说，+ 情况
explanation: These phrases introduce a point of view. 对我来说 and 在他看来 mean "for me" and "in his opinion", 看来 means "it seems", and 一般来说 means "generally speaking". Put them at the start of the sentence, followed by a comma.

examples.pinyin: duì wǒ lái shuō, hàn zì hěn nán.
examples.en: For me, Chinese characters are hard.

examples.pinyin: kàn lái yào xià yǔ le.
examples.en: It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.pinyin: yì bān lái shuō, zhōu mò rén hěn duō.
examples.en: Generally speaking, there are a lot of people on weekends.

mistake.pinyin: duì wǒ lái shuō, hàn zì hěn nán.
mistake.en: For me, Chinese characters are hard.
mistake.reason: Don't mix the two frames: use 对……来说 or 在……看来, not 对……看来.

title: 越来越 / 越……越……
pattern: A 越来越 + adj / A 越 V1 越 adj
explanation: 越来越 + adjective means 'more and more' and shows a change over time. 越 A 越 B means 'the more A, the more B'. Do not put 很 after 越.

examples.pinyin: tiān qì yuè lái yuè lěng
examples.en: The weather is getting colder and colder.

examples.pinyin: yǔ yuè xià yuè dà
examples.en: The rain is falling harder and harder.

examples.pinyin: tā yuè shuō yuè gāo xìng
examples.en: The more he talks, the happier he gets.

mistake.pinyin: tiān qì yuè lái yuè lěng
mistake.en: The weather is getting colder and colder.
mistake.reason: Do not add 很 after 越来越; the adjective follows directly.

title: 一……也 / 都 + 不 / 没……
pattern: 一 + 量词 (+ 名词) + 也 / 都 + 不 / 没 + 动词
explanation: Put 一 plus a measure word before 也 or 都, then add 不 or 没, to say "not even one", meaning none at all. Use 没 for things that did not happen or do not exist, and 不 for states and habits.

examples.pinyin: wǒ yì kǒu dōu méi chī
examples.en: I didn't eat a single bite.

examples.pinyin: jīntiān wǒ yìdiǎnr yě bú lèi
examples.en: I'm not tired at all today.

examples.pinyin: jiàoshì lǐ yí gè rén yě méiyǒu
examples.en: There isn't a single person in the classroom.

mistake.pinyin: wǒ yí cì yě méi qù guo
mistake.en: I have never gone even once.
mistake.reason: This pattern needs a negative word (没 or 不) after 也 or 都, even though the English sounds like "not even once" without it.

title: 从……起
pattern: 从 + time + 起，clause
explanation: 从……起 marks the point in time when something begins and then continues. Put the starting time between 从 and 起, then say what happens from then on.

examples.pinyin: cóng míngtiān qǐ, wǒ měitiān pǎobù.
examples.en: Starting tomorrow, I will run every day.

examples.zh: 从今天起，我不喝牛奶了。
examples.pinyin: cóng jīntiān qǐ, wǒ bù hē niúnǎi le.
examples.en: From today on, I won't drink milk anymore.

examples.zh: 从那天起，他再也没来过。
examples.pinyin: cóng nà tiān qǐ, tā zài yě méi lái guo.
examples.en: From that day on, he never came again.

mistake.pinyin: cóng míngtiān qǐ, wǒ měitiān pǎobù.
mistake.en: Starting tomorrow, I will run every day.
mistake.reason: You need 从 before the time word and 起 after it, not 起 before it.

title: 该……了
pattern: 该 + (person) + verb + 了 / 该 + person + 了
explanation: Use 该……了 to say it is now time for someone to do something. You can also use 该你了 to say it is someone's turn.

examples.pinyin: wǒ gāi zǒu le
examples.en: I should get going now.

examples.pinyin: bā diǎn le gāi qǐ chuáng le
examples.en: It's eight o'clock, time to get up.

examples.pinyin: gāi nǐ le nǐ lái shuō ba
examples.en: It's your turn, you go ahead and speak.

mistake.pinyin: wǒ gāi huí jiā le
mistake.en: It's time for me to go home.
mistake.reason: Without 了, 该 only means 'should'; add 了 to say the time has come now.

title: 在……上 / 下 / 中
pattern: 在 + noun + 上 / 下 / 中, + clause
explanation: This frame sets the scope or condition of a statement. 在……上 means 'in terms of / in the area of', 在……下 means 'under the help or conditions of', and 在……中 means 'in the process or setting of'.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài xuéxí shang hěn nǔlì.
examples.en: He works hard in terms of study.

examples.zh: 在大家的帮助下,我学会了汉语。
examples.pinyin: Zài dàjiā de bāngzhù xià, wǒ xuéhuì le Hànyǔ.
examples.en: With everyone's help, I learned Chinese.

examples.zh: 在生活中,我常常说汉语。
examples.pinyin: Zài shēnghuó zhōng, wǒ chángcháng shuō Hànyǔ.
examples.en: In daily life, I often speak Chinese.

mistake.wrong: 在大家的帮助上,我找到了工作。
mistake.right: 在大家的帮助下,我找到了工作。
mistake.pinyin: Zài dàjiā de bāngzhù xià, wǒ zhǎodào le gōngzuò.
mistake.en: With everyone's help, I found a job.
mistake.reason: For 'with help from', the fixed frame is 在……下, not 在……上.

title: 看起来 / 看上去
pattern: A 看起来 / 看上去 + adj
explanation: Use 看起来 or 看上去 to say how someone or something seems based on how it looks. Put it after the subject and before the adjective.

examples.pinyin: Tā kànqǐlái hěn lèi.
examples.en: He looks very tired.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu kànshàngqù hěn guì.
examples.en: This piece of clothing looks expensive.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jīntiān kànqǐlái hěn gāoxìng.
examples.en: You look very happy today.

mistake.pinyin: Tā kànqǐlái hěn lèi.
mistake.en: He looks very tired.
mistake.reason: Do not add 是 after 看起来; go straight to the adjective.

title: 需要 / 应该 / 该 / 愿意 / 得 děi
pattern: S + 需要/应该/该/愿意/得 + V；否定：不需要/不应该/不愿意/不用
explanation: 需要 means need, 应该 and 该 mean should, 愿意 means be willing, and 得 (děi) means must or have to. For negatives, use 不需要, 不应该 and 不愿意; to say you don't have to, use 不用, never 不得.

examples.pinyin: nǐ xū yào xiū xi
examples.en: You need to rest.

examples.pinyin: nǐ yīng gāi zǎo diǎnr shuì
examples.en: You should sleep a bit earlier.

examples.pinyin: wǒ yuàn yì bāng nǐ
examples.en: I am willing to help you.

mistake.wrong: 明天不是星期天，你不得来上班。
mistake.right: 明天不是星期天，你得来上班。
mistake.pinyin: míng tiān bú shì xīng qī tiān, nǐ děi lái shàng bān
mistake.en: Tomorrow is not Sunday, you have to come to work.
mistake.reason: 得 (děi) has no regular negative; but for not having to, say 不用, as in 你不用来上班 (you don't need to come to work).

title: Separable verbs
pattern: V + 了/过 + (amount) + O  |  跟 + person + V-O
explanation: Separable verbs are verb + object words, like 见面 and 上班. Put 了, 过 or amounts between the two parts, and never add a direct object after them. Use 跟 or 给 before the verb to bring in the other person.

examples.pinyin: wǒmen jiàn guo miàn
examples.en: We have met before.

examples.pinyin: tā bāng le wǒ yí gè máng
examples.en: He did me a favor.

examples.zh: 我今天上了四个小时班。
examples.pinyin: wǒ jīntiān shàng le sì gè xiǎoshí bān
examples.en: I worked four hours today.

mistake.pinyin: wǒ zuótiān gēn tā jiànmiàn
mistake.en: I met him yesterday.
mistake.reason: 见面 already contains its object, so the person must come before the verb with 跟.

title: 才 and 就 with time
pattern: Time + 才 + Verb (late) / Time + 就 + Verb + 了 (early)
explanation: Put 才 after a time word to show something happened later or more slowly than expected. Put 就 after a time word to show it happened earlier or sooner than expected, and usually add 了.

examples.pinyin: Tā shí diǎn cái qǐchuáng.
examples.en: He didn't get up until ten o'clock.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ liù diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
examples.en: I got up as early as six o'clock.

examples.pinyin: Māma wǎnshang jiǔ diǎn cái xiàbān.
examples.en: Mom doesn't get off work until nine at night.

mistake.pinyin: Wǒ liù diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
mistake.en: I got up as early as six o'clock.
mistake.reason: Use 就 (with 了) for something earlier than expected; 才 means late and doesn't take 了.

title: 刚 / 刚刚 / 一直 / 马上 / 终于
pattern: 刚(刚) / 一直 / 马上 / 终于 + verb
explanation: These adverbs go before the verb. 刚(刚) means just now, 一直 means all along, 马上 means right away, and 终于 means finally.

examples.pinyin: wǒ gāng dào jiā
examples.en: I just got home.

examples.pinyin: tā yìzhí zài děng nǐ
examples.en: He has been waiting for you all along.

examples.pinyin: nǐ děng yíxià wǒ mǎshàng lái
examples.en: Wait a moment, I'll come right away.

mistake.pinyin: tā zhōngyú lái le
mistake.en: He finally came.
mistake.reason: 终于 is an adverb and must go before the verb, not after it.

title: Adverbs of likelihood and certainty
pattern: Subject + 大概/好像/差不多/几乎/一定/必须/当然/其实 + Verb/Adj
explanation: These adverbs go after the subject and before the verb or adjective. 大概 and 好像 mean 'probably/seems', 差不多 and 几乎 mean 'almost', 一定 and 必须 mean 'definitely/must', 当然 means 'of course', and 其实 means 'actually'.

examples.pinyin: Tā hǎoxiàng bìng le.
examples.en: He seems to be sick.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bìxū qù yīyuàn.
examples.en: You must go to the hospital.

examples.pinyin: Qíshí wǒ bù xǐhuan kāfēi.
examples.en: Actually, I don't like coffee.

mistake.wrong: 好像他病了,大概明天我去。
mistake.right: 他好像病了,我明天大概去。
mistake.pinyin: Tā hǎoxiàng bìng le, wǒ míngtiān dàgài qù.
mistake.en: He seems to be sick, and I will probably go tomorrow.
mistake.reason: Place the adverb after the subject and right before the verb, not at the start of the sentence like in English.

title: 挺 / 特别 / 有些 / 比较
pattern: 挺/特别/有些/比较 + adj (挺 + adj + 的)
explanation: Put these degree adverbs before an adjective: 挺 (quite), 特别 (especially), 有些 (somewhat, a bit negative), 比较 (relatively). 挺……的 is colloquial and often ends with 的.

examples.pinyin: jīn tiān tiān qì tǐng hǎo de
examples.en: The weather is quite nice today.

examples.pinyin: wǒ jīn tiān tè bié gāo xìng
examples.en: I am especially happy today.

examples.pinyin: tā yǒu xiē lèi
examples.en: He is a bit tired.

mistake.pinyin: wǒ jiā bǐ jiào yuǎn
mistake.en: My home is relatively far.
mistake.reason: Use only one degree adverb before the adjective; don't stack 挺 and 很.

title: Reduplicated measure words
pattern: Measure word reduplicated (个个, 张张) = 'every one'; 一 + M + 一 + M + 地 + verb = 'one by one'
explanation: Repeating a measure word (个个, 本本, 件件) means 'every single one', and it is usually followed by 都. Repeating 一 + measure word with 地 before the verb (一个一个地) means doing something 'one by one'.

examples.zh: 我们班的学生个个都很高兴。
examples.pinyin: wǒ men bān de xué shēng gè gè dōu hěn gāo xìng
examples.en: Every student in our class is very happy.

examples.pinyin: zhè xiē shū běn běn dōu hěn hǎo kàn
examples.en: Every one of these books is good.

examples.zh: 孩子们一个一个地进来了。
examples.pinyin: hái zi men yí gè yí gè de jìn lái le
examples.en: The children came in one by one.

mistake.right: 这些衣服件件都很好看。
mistake.pinyin: zhè xiē yī fu jiàn jiàn dōu hěn hǎo kàn
mistake.en: Every one of these clothes looks good.
mistake.reason: A reduplicated measure word means 'every one', so it needs 都 before the verb or adjective phrase.

title: Approximate numbers with 大概 or two numbers
pattern: 大概 + number + M + N  /  number1 number2 + M + N
explanation: To give a rough amount, put 大概 before the number, or say two neighbouring numbers together (三四, 七八). Two-number style goes directly before the measure word.

examples.zh: 我们公司大概有五十个人。
examples.pinyin: wǒ men gōng sī dà gài yǒu wǔ shí gè rén 。
examples.en: Our company has about fifty people.

examples.pinyin: wǒ xiǎng xiū xi liǎng sān tiān 。
examples.en: I want to rest for two or three days.

examples.pinyin: tā de nǚ ér shí wǔ liù suì 。
examples.en: His daughter is fifteen or sixteen years old.

mistake.wrong: 我有三五个朋友在纽约。
mistake.right: 我有三四个朋友在纽约。
mistake.pinyin: wǒ yǒu sān sì gè péng you zài niǔ yuē 。
mistake.en: I have three or four friends in New York.
mistake.reason: Use two consecutive numbers (三四), not numbers that skip one (三五).
